title: Spatial interpolation with climaemet
text: Prediction unobserved locations requires spatial interpolation. example, use terra apply inverse distance weighting method, one several spatial interpolation approaches. See Hijmans (2023) detailed explanation analysis R. process follows: Create spatial object (SpatRaster) store predicted values. Interpolate observations. Visualize results. analysis requires destination object representing locations predict. common approach create spatial grid (raster) covers target area. example, use terra create regular grid use interpolation. important consideration spatial analysis visualization coordinate reference system (CRS). cover detail article, mention key points: using multiple spatial objects, ensure use CRS. can achieved projecting objects (.e. transforming coordinates) CRS. Longitude/latitude coordinates unprojected. project object (example, Mercator projection), change x/y values every point. projection transforms coordinates. measure distance meters, choose projection appropriate region. Distances longitude/latitude uniform: one degree longitude 111 km equator much smaller near poles. Degrees divide circle equal angular segments, Earth’s meridians converge toward poles, ground distances vary latitude. exercise, choose project objects ETRS89 / UTM zone 30N EPSG:25830, provides x y values meters suitable study area. Create regular grid terra. grid contains equally spaced cells across bounding box Spain. use resolution 5,000 m, grid cells 5 5 km (25 square km): Populate empty grid values predicted observations: Figure 2: Example: IDW interpolation Create polished ggplot2 plot. See Royé (2020) examples. Figure 3: Average temperature Spain (2021-01-08, interpolated)
code: clim_data_utm <- st_transform(clim_data_clean, 25830) ccaa_utm <- st_transform(ccaa_esp, 25830)  # Note the original projection.  st_crs(ccaa_esp)$proj4string #> [1] "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs"  # Compare it with the UTM projection.  st_crs(ccaa_utm)$proj4string #> [1] "+proj=utm +zone=30 +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs" # Create a 5 by 5 km grid (25 square km).  grd <- rast(ccaa_utm, res = c(5000, 5000))  # Count cells.  ncell(grd) #> [1] 44004 # Test with a single day.  test_day <- clim_data_utm |> filter(fecha == "2021-01-08")  # Interpolate temperature. init_p <- test_day |>   vect() |>   as_tibble(geom = "XY")  gs <- gstat(   formula = tmed ~ 1,   locations = ~ x + y,   data = init_p,   set = list(idp = 2) )  interp_temp <- interpolate(grd, gs) #> [inverse distance weighted interpolation] #> [inverse distance weighted interpolation]  # Plot with tidyterra. ggplot() +   geom_spatraster(data = select(interp_temp, var1.pred)) +   scale_fill_whitebox_c(     palette = "bl_yl_rd",     labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "°C")   ) +   labs(     title = "(interpolated) temperature",     subtitle = "2021-01-08"   ) # Create a polished ggplot2 plot. temp_values <- interp_temp |>   pull(var1.pred) |>   range(na.rm = TRUE)  # Get minimum and maximum interpolated values. min_temp <- floor(min(temp_values)) max_temp <- ceiling(max(temp_values))  ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = ccaa_utm, fill = "grey95") +   geom_spatraster(data = select(interp_temp, var1.pred)) +   scale_fill_gradientn(     colours = hcl.colors(11, "Spectral", rev = TRUE, alpha = 0.7),     limits = c(min_temp, max_temp)   ) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Average temperature in Spain",     subtitle = "2021-01-08",     caption = "Data: AEMET, IGN",     fill = "°C"   )

text: section, loop dates create single SpatRaster several layers, one holding interpolation specific date. , create animation show temperature changes winter 2020–2021. Inspect results: Figure 4: Temperatures (selected) Finally, loop layers produce one PNG file per date. combine PNG files GIF gifski. Use gifski create animation: Figure 5: Animation average temperature Spain, Dec 2020-Mar 2021
code: # Create a SpatRaster with a layer for each date. dates <- sort(unique(clim_data_clean$fecha))  # Loop through days and create interpolations. interp_list <- lapply(dates, function(x) {   thisdate <- x   tmp_day <- clim_data_utm |>     filter(fecha == thisdate) |>     vect() |>     as_tibble(geom = "XY")    gs_day <- gstat(formula = tmed ~ 1, locations = ~ x + y, data = tmp_day)   interp_day <- interpolate(grd, gs_day, idp = 2.0) |>     select(interpolated = var1.pred)    names(interp_day) <- format(thisdate)    interp_day })  # Concatenate to a single SpatRaster. interp_rast <- do.call(c, interp_list) |> mask(vect(ccaa_utm))  time(interp_rast) <- dates interp_rast #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 193, 228, 90  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 5000.706, 5006.959  (x, y) #> extent      : -13882.95, 1126278, 3892802, 4859145  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : ETRS89 / UTM zone 30N (EPSG:25830) #> source(s)   : memory #> names       : 2020-12-21, 2020-12-22, 2020-12-23, 2020-12-24, 2020-12-25, 2020-12-26, ... #> min values  :   0.844198,   4.199887,   2.470233,  -1.814927,     -7.807,  -9.228323, ... #> max values  :  18.997771,   18.86457,  16.683431,  16.854208,  16.010724,  14.617574, ... #> time (days) : 2020-12-21 to 2021-03-20 (90 steps)  nlyr(interp_rast) #> [1] 90  head(names(interp_rast)) #> [1] "2020-12-21" "2020-12-22" "2020-12-23" "2020-12-24" "2020-12-25" #> [6] "2020-12-26"  # Create a faceted map with selected dates.  ggplot() +   geom_spatraster(data = select(interp_rast, 1:16)) +   facet_wrap(~lyr) +   scale_fill_whitebox_c(palette = "pi_y_g", alpha = 1) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(axis.text = element_blank()) +   labs(title = "Temperatures (selected)") # Extend and animate the results. # Create GIF.  # Use a common scale from all observed values in each layer. allvalues <- values(interp_rast, mat = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)  min_temp2 <- floor(min(allvalues)) max_temp2 <- ceiling(max(allvalues))  # Loop through all the layers. all_layers <- names(interp_rast)  for (i in seq_along(all_layers)) {   # Create a GIF for each date.   this <- all_layers[i]   interp_rast_day <- interp_rast |> select(all_of(this))    this_date <- as.Date(gsub("interp_", "", this, fixed = TRUE))    g <- ggplot() +     geom_spatraster(data = interp_rast_day) +     geom_sf(data = ccaa_utm, fill = NA) +     coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +     scale_fill_gradientn(       colours = hcl.colors(20, "Spectral", rev = TRUE, alpha = 0.8),       limits = c(min_temp2, max_temp2),       na.value = NA,       labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "°C")     ) +     theme_minimal() +     labs(       title = "Average temperature in Spain",       subtitle = this_date,       caption = "Data: AEMET, IGN",       fill = ""     )    tmp <- file.path(tempdir(), paste0(this, ".png"))   ggsave(tmp, g, width = 1600, height = 1200, units = "px", bg = "white") } # Create GIF from temporary PNGs. allfiles <- file.path(tempdir(), paste0(all_layers, ".png")) gifski::gifski(   allfiles,   loop = TRUE,   delay = 1 / 6,   gif_file = "winter_2021.gif",   width = 1600,   height = 1200 )

code: # Plot warming stripes for a weather station.  library(ggplot2)  # Load example data. temp_data <- climaemet::climaemet_9434_temp  ggstripes(temp_data, plot_title = "Zaragoza Airport") +   labs(subtitle = "(1950-2020)") # Plot a Walter-Lieth climate diagram for a weather station.  # Load example data. wl_data <- climaemet::climaemet_9434_climatogram  ggclimat_walter_lieth(   wl_data,   alt = "249",   per = "1981-2010",   est = "Zaragoza Airport" ) # Plot a wind rose for a weather station.  # Load example data. wind_data <- climaemet::climaemet_9434_wind  speed <- wind_data$velmedia direction <- wind_data$dir  ggwindrose(   speed = speed,   direction = direction,   speed_cuts = seq(0, 16, 4),   legend_title = "Wind speed (m/s)",   calm_wind = 0,   n_col = 1,   plot_title = "Zaragoza Airport" ) +   labs(subtitle = "2000-2020", caption = "Source: AEMET")
